why: The statement asks only whether srg(99,14,1,2) exists, so a nonexistence result restricted to a class of graphs (by automorphism group, or circulant on Z/99) is a case. Thakkar v1's circulant exhaustion is such a case. I treated it as checkable because it is a finite, decisive enumeration that anyone can rerun. Its forced-structure reduction is a reformulation, and its 69.43% artifact is a partial-score search, not a bound on the problem. The v1 disclosure says Claude generated the implementation of the circulant bound and the reduction, while the strategy came from the author. That puts mathematics in the result as computational work the agent built and ran, so I answered assisted rather than generated or none. v2 adds new mathematics only in the 70.73% artifact. The authors say it is not a bound and not evidence either way, so its scope is none, even though AlphaEvolve generated it. Both Reimbayev papers are conditional or structural and settle nothing for n=99. Keramatipour is a negative result about a method. Zehavi–de Oliveira solves an alternative question. I read the restricted nonexistence results as going against existence (refuted) within their class.
doubts: The Thakkar v1 AI role was a close call between assisted and none. The quote says the agent 'generated' the implementation of the circulant bound and the reduction, and the strategy was human, which is why I chose assisted. I chose checkable for the circulant ceiling even though the record did not confirm that the code was released. The unlocated Makhnev nonexistence attribution in Reimbayev's papers is unresolved. The Keramatipour date may really be June 2023 if the thesis was public then, but this does not matter because its scope is none.
